DEU.P.3.23-29.text: Moses Forbidden to Cross the Jordan

DEU.P.13.1-11.text: Idolaters to Be Put to Death

DEU.P.16.1-8.text: Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread

DEU.P.19.15-21.text: The Testimony of Two or Three Witnesses

DEU.P.21.22-23.text: Cursed Is Anyone Hung on a Tree

DEU.P.30.11-20.text: The Choice of Life or Death

DEU.P.31.24-29.text: The Law Placed in the Ark

DEU.1.1-2.text: Moses speaks to Israel east of the Jordan

DEU.1.3-4.text: Moses tells the Israelites what the LORD commanded

DEU.1.5-6.text: Moses begins to explain the law in Moab

DEU.1.7-8.text: The LORD tells Israel to enter and possess the land

DEU.1.9-11.text: Moses says he cannot carry the burden of Israel alone

DEU.1.12-14.text: Moses asks Israel to choose wise men as leaders

DEU.1.15-16.text: Moses appoints leaders and charges the judges

DEU.1.17-18.text: Moses tells the judges to be fair and not afraid

DEU.1.19-19.text: Israel travels from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea

DEU.1.20-21.text: Moses tells Israel to take the land without fear

DEU.1.22-24.text: Moses sends twelve men to spy out the land

DEU.1.25-25.text: The spies bring back fruit and a good report

DEU.1.26-28.text: Israel rebels and is afraid to enter the land

DEU.1.29-31.text: Moses tells Israel not to fear because God fights

DEU.1.32-33.text: Israel does not trust the LORD who led the way

DEU.1.34-36.text: The LORD swears that only Caleb will see the land

DEU.1.37-38.text: Moses cannot enter the land; Joshua will enter

DEU.1.39-40.text: The children will enter the land; adults must turn back

DEU.1.41-42.text: Israel plans to fight, but the LORD says not to

DEU.1.43-44.text: Israel disobeys and the Amorites defeat Israel

DEU.1.45-46.text: Israel weeps, but the LORD does not listen

DEU.2.1-3.text: Israel wanders near Mount Seir, then turns north

DEU.2.4-5.text: Israel must not fight the descendants of Esau

DEU.2.6-7.text: Israel must pay for food and water; God has provided

DEU.2.8-8.text: Israel passes by the descendants of Esau

DEU.2.9-9.text: The LORD tells Israel not to fight the Moabites

DEU.2.10-11.text: The Emites, a tall people, once lived in Moab

DEU.2.12-12.text: The descendants of Esau drove out the Horites

DEU.2.13-15.text: Israel crosses the Zered as the old generation dies

DEU.2.16-19.text: The LORD tells Israel not to fight the Ammonites

DEU.2.20-22.text: The Ammonites drove out the Zamzummites

DEU.2.23-23.text: The Caphtorites destroyed the Avvim near Gaza

DEU.2.24-25.text: The LORD gives Sihon and his land to Israel

DEU.2.26-27.text: Moses offers peace to Sihon king of Heshbon

DEU.2.28-29.text: Moses asks Sihon to let Israel pass and buy food

DEU.2.30-31.text: Sihon refuses, and the LORD says to begin taking his land

DEU.2.32-33.text: Israel defeats Sihon and his army at Jahaz

DEU.2.34-35.text: Israel captures Sihon’s cities and keeps the livestock

DEU.2.36-37.text: The LORD gives Israel every city, but Israel avoids Ammon

DEU.3.1-2.text: The LORD tells Moses not to fear Og king of Bashan

DEU.3.3-4.text: Israel defeats Og and captures all sixty of his cities

DEU.3.5-7.text: Israel destroys the people of Og’s walled cities

DEU.3.8-10.text: Israel takes the land east of the Jordan from two kings

DEU.3.11-11.text: Og’s iron bed shows he was the last of the Rephaim

DEU.3.12-13.text: Moses gives the conquered land to Reuben, Gad and Manasseh

DEU.3.14-14.text: Jair takes the region of Argob and names it after himself

DEU.3.15-16.text: Moses gives Gilead to Machir and land to Reuben and Gad

DEU.3.17-17.text: Moses describes the western border along the Jordan

DEU.3.18-18.text: Moses tells the fighting men to cross ahead of their brothers

DEU.3.19-20.text: Wives and children may stay until all Israel has its land

DEU.3.21-22.text: Moses tells Joshua not to fear, because the LORD will fight

DEU.3.23-25.text: Moses begs the LORD to let him cross the Jordan

DEU.3.26-27.text: The LORD refuses Moses and tells him to view the land

DEU.3.28-29.text: The LORD tells Moses to encourage Joshua to lead the people

DEU.4.1-2.text: Moses tells Israel to obey the laws and not change them

DEU.4.3-4.text: Moses reminds Israel what happened at Baal-peor

DEU.4.5-6.text: Moses says obeying the laws will show Israel’s wisdom

DEU.4.7-8.text: Moses says no other nation has a god so near or laws so right

DEU.4.9-10.text: Moses tells Israel not to forget and to teach their children

DEU.4.11-12.text: Moses recalls the LORD speaking from the fire at the mountain

DEU.4.13-14.text: Moses recalls the Ten Commandments and the laws he must teach

DEU.4.15-18.text: Moses warns Israel not to make any idol in any form

DEU.4.19-20.text: Moses warns Israel not to worship the sun, moon and stars

DEU.4.21-22.text: Moses says he will die before crossing, but Israel will cross

DEU.4.23-24.text: Moses warns Israel to keep the covenant and make no idols

DEU.4.25-26.text: Moses warns that idols will bring Israel’s destruction in the land

DEU.4.27-28.text: Moses warns that the LORD will scatter Israel among the nations

DEU.4.29-29.text: Israel will find the LORD if they seek him with all their heart

DEU.4.30-31.text: Moses says Israel will return to the merciful LORD

DEU.4.32-33.text: Moses reminds Israel that God spoke from the fire

DEU.4.34-34.text: No other god ever rescued a nation as the LORD did

DEU.4.35-36.text: The LORD showed Israel that he alone is God

DEU.4.37-38.text: Because of love, the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt

DEU.4.39-40.text: Moses urges Israel to know the LORD is God and obey

DEU.4.44-46.text: Moses sets the law before Israel east of the Jordan

DEU.4.47-49.text: Israel took the land of Sihon and Og east of the Jordan

DEU.5.1-3.text: Moses calls Israel to learn and obey the LORD’s laws

DEU.5.4-4.text: The LORD spoke to Israel face to face from the fire

DEU.5.5-6.text: Moses speaks the LORD’s word because Israel feared the fire

DEU.5.7-8.text: The LORD tells Israel to have no other gods or idols

DEU.5.9-10.text: Israel must not worship idols, for the LORD is jealous

DEU.5.11-11.text: Israel must not misuse the name of the LORD

DEU.5.12-14.text: Israel must keep the Sabbath as a day of rest for all

DEU.5.15-15.text: Israel keeps the Sabbath to remember slavery in Egypt

DEU.5.16-16.text: Children must honor father and mother

DEU.5.17-20.text: Israel must not murder, commit adultery, steal or lie

DEU.5.21-21.text: Israel must not covet a neighbor’s wife or property

DEU.5.22-22.text: The LORD gave the commandments on two stone tablets

DEU.5.23-24.text: Israel’s leaders tell Moses God has shown his glory

DEU.5.25-27.text: The Israelites fear God’s voice and ask Moses to go near

DEU.5.28-30.text: The LORD approves what Israel said and sends Israel home

DEU.5.31-31.text: The LORD tells Moses to stay and receive all the laws

DEU.5.32-33.text: Moses urges Israel to obey the LORD and not turn aside

DEU.6.1-2.text: Moses teaches Israel to fear the LORD and keep his laws

DEU.6.3-3.text: Moses tells Israel to obey and prosper in the land

DEU.6.4-5.text: Israel must love the one LORD with everything

DEU.6.6-7.text: Moses tells parents to teach God’s words to children

DEU.6.8-9.text: Israel must keep God’s words on hands, heads and doors

DEU.6.10-12.text: In the good land, Israel must not forget the LORD

DEU.6.13-15.text: Israel must serve only the LORD and not follow other gods

DEU.6.16-17.text: Israel must not test the LORD and must keep his commands

DEU.6.18-19.text: Israel must do what is right to enter the good land

DEU.6.20-23.text: Parents tell children how the LORD freed Israel from Egypt

DEU.6.24-25.text: Israel will be righteous by obeying the LORD’s commands

DEU.7.1-1.text: The LORD will drive out seven nations for Israel

DEU.7.2-3.text: Israel must not make treaties or intermarry with the nations

DEU.7.4-5.text: Israel must tear down altars and burn idols

DEU.7.6-6.text: Israel is a holy people chosen by the LORD

DEU.7.7-8.text: The LORD chose Israel because of his love, not its size

DEU.7.9-11.text: The LORD is faithful; Israel must keep his commands

DEU.7.12-13.text: The LORD will bless Israel if Israel keeps his laws

DEU.7.14-15.text: The LORD will bless Israel and remove sickness

DEU.7.16-16.text: Israel must show no pity and not worship the peoples’ gods

DEU.7.17-19.text: Israel should not fear the nations, but remember Egypt

DEU.7.20-22.text: The LORD will drive out the nations little by little

DEU.7.23-24.text: The LORD will give the nations’ kings to Israel

DEU.7.25-26.text: Israel must burn idols and bring none into the house

DEU.8.1-2.text: Israel must obey and remember forty years in the wilderness

DEU.8.3-3.text: God gave Israel manna to teach that people live by his word

DEU.8.4-6.text: The LORD disciplines Israel like a father; Israel must obey

DEU.8.7-8.text: The LORD is bringing Israel into a good land

DEU.8.9-10.text: The good land will lack nothing; Israel must bless the LORD

DEU.8.11-12.text: Israel must not forget the LORD when life is good

DEU.8.13-14.text: Wealth may make Israel proud and forget the LORD

DEU.8.15-17.text: Israel must not say that its own power brought wealth

DEU.8.18-20.text: Israel will perish if Israel forgets the LORD

DEU.9.1-2.text: Israel will cross the Jordan to face strong nations

DEU.9.3-3.text: The LORD will go ahead of Israel like a consuming fire

DEU.9.4-4.text: The LORD drives out the nations because of wickedness

DEU.9.5-5.text: Israel is not righteous; the LORD keeps his promise

DEU.9.6-6.text: Israel is a stiff-necked people, not righteous

DEU.9.7-8.text: Moses reminds Israel how Israel rebelled against the LORD

DEU.9.9-10.text: Moses stays forty days on the mountain and receives tablets

DEU.9.11-12.text: The LORD tells Moses that Israel has made a molten image

DEU.9.13-14.text: The LORD says he will destroy Israel and make Moses great

DEU.9.15-16.text: Moses comes down and sees the molten calf Israel made

DEU.9.17-18.text: Moses breaks the tablets and prays forty days

DEU.9.19-20.text: Moses prays for Aaron and the LORD listens

DEU.9.21-21.text: Moses destroys the calf and throws the dust in a stream

DEU.9.22-24.text: Moses reminds Israel of more rebellion against the LORD

DEU.9.25-26.text: Moses prays again that the LORD will not destroy Israel

DEU.9.27-29.text: Moses asks the LORD to remember Abraham, Isaac and Jacob

DEU.10.1-2.text: The LORD tells Moses to make new tablets and an ark

DEU.10.3-4.text: Moses makes the ark and the LORD writes on new tablets

DEU.10.5-5.text: Moses puts the tablets in the ark

DEU.10.6-7.text: Israel travels; Aaron dies and Eleazar becomes priest

DEU.10.8-9.text: The LORD sets apart the Levites for service

DEU.10.10-11.text: The LORD spares Israel and tells Moses to lead on

DEU.10.12-13.text: Moses asks Israel to fear, love and serve the LORD

DEU.10.14-15.text: The LORD owns everything, yet chose and loved Israel

DEU.10.16-17.text: Israel must stop being stubborn; the LORD is fair

DEU.10.18-19.text: God helps orphans and widows; Israel must love foreigners

DEU.10.20-21.text: Moses tells Israel to fear and hold fast to the LORD

DEU.10.22-22.text: The LORD has made Israel grow from seventy to many

DEU.11.1-1.text: Moses tells Israel to love and obey the LORD

DEU.11.2-3.text: Moses reminds Israel of what the LORD did in Egypt

DEU.11.4-5.text: Moses reminds Israel of the Red Sea and the wilderness

DEU.11.6-7.text: The earth swallowed Dathan and Abiram

DEU.11.8-9.text: Israel must obey to enter and keep the land

DEU.11.10-12.text: The new land needs rain, and the LORD cares for it

DEU.11.13-15.text: The LORD promises rain and food if Israel obeys

DEU.11.16-17.text: Moses warns Israel not to worship other gods

DEU.11.18-19.text: Israel must keep God’s words in mind and teach children

DEU.11.20-21.text: Israel must write God’s words on doors and gates

DEU.11.22-23.text: The LORD will drive out nations if Israel obeys

DEU.11.24-25.text: The LORD promises Israel all the land and victory

DEU.11.26-28.text: Moses sets a blessing and a curse before Israel

DEU.11.29-30.text: Israel will proclaim blessing on Gerizim and curse on Ebal

DEU.11.31-32.text: Moses tells Israel to obey the laws in the new land

DEU.12.1-2.text: Israel must destroy the places where nations worship gods

DEU.12.3-4.text: Israel must destroy the altars and idols of the nations

DEU.12.5-6.text: Israel must bring offerings to the place God chooses

DEU.12.7-7.text: Israelite families will eat and rejoice before the LORD

DEU.12.8-9.text: Israel has not yet reached the resting place God gives

DEU.12.10-11.text: In the land, Israel will bring offerings to one place

DEU.12.12-12.text: Israel must rejoice before the LORD with the Levites

DEU.12.13-14.text: Israel must offer burnt offerings only where God chooses

DEU.12.15-16.text: Israelites may eat meat at home but must not eat blood

DEU.12.17-17.text: Israel must not eat the tithes and offerings at home

DEU.12.18-19.text: Israel must eat the offerings at God’s chosen place

DEU.12.20-20.text: When God enlarges the land, Israel may eat meat freely

DEU.12.21-22.text: If God’s place is far, Israel may eat meat at home

DEU.12.23-25.text: Israel must not eat blood, because blood is life

DEU.12.26-27.text: Israel must take holy gifts to the place God chooses

DEU.12.28-28.text: Moses tells Israel to obey so that all goes well

DEU.12.29-30.text: Israel must not copy the gods of the nations

DEU.12.31-32.text: Israel must not worship God as nations worship idols

DEU.13.1-3.text: Israel must not follow a prophet who urges other gods

DEU.13.4-5.text: A prophet who leads Israel away from God must die

DEU.13.6-7.text: A family member or friend may urge worship of other gods

DEU.13.8-9.text: Israel must put to death anyone who urges idol worship

DEU.13.10-11.text: All Israel will hear and fear when idolaters are stoned

DEU.13.12-14.text: Israel must check reports of a city worshiping idols

DEU.13.15-16.text: Israel must burn the city and its plunder completely

DEU.13.17-18.text: If Israel keeps nothing from the city, God will show mercy

DEU.14.1-2.text: Israel is God’s holy people, so no cutting for the dead

DEU.14.3-5.text: Moses lists the animals that Israel may eat

DEU.14.6-7.text: Israel may not eat the camel, rabbit or rock badger

DEU.14.8-8.text: Israel must not eat pig meat or touch a dead pig

DEU.14.9-10.text: Israel may eat only water animals with fins and scales

DEU.14.11-13.text: Israel may eat clean birds but not eagles and vultures

DEU.14.14-17.text: Israel must not eat ravens, owls, hawks and other birds

DEU.14.18-20.text: Israel must not eat storks, bats or flying insects

DEU.14.21-21.text: Israel is holy and must not eat an animal found dead

DEU.14.22-23.text: Israel must set aside a tenth and eat it before the LORD

DEU.14.24-25.text: Israelites may sell the tithe for money if the way is far

DEU.14.26-27.text: Israelites may buy food for a feast and remember the Levite

DEU.14.28-29.text: Every third year the tithe feeds Levites and the needy

DEU.15.1-3.text: Every seventh year Israelites must cancel debts

DEU.15.4-6.text: God promises to bless Israel if the people obey him

DEU.15.7-8.text: Israelites must freely lend to a poor brother

DEU.15.9-10.text: Israelites must give to the poor without a grudge

DEU.15.11-11.text: There will always be poor, so Israelites must give freely

DEU.15.12-14.text: Israelites must free servants after six years with gifts

DEU.15.15-17.text: A servant who loves his master may stay for life

DEU.15.18-18.text: Israelites should not see freeing a servant as a hardship

DEU.15.19-21.text: Israelites must give firstborn male animals to the LORD

DEU.15.22-23.text: Israelites may eat the animal at home but not the blood

DEU.16.1-2.text: Israelites must celebrate Passover in the month of Abib

DEU.16.3-4.text: Israelites must eat unleavened bread for seven days

DEU.16.5-6.text: Israelites must offer the Passover only at the chosen place

DEU.16.7-8.text: Israelites roast the Passover and hold a solemn assembly

DEU.16.9-10.text: Israelites must keep the Feast of Weeks with a gift

DEU.16.11-12.text: Israelites must rejoice with servants, Levites and the poor

DEU.16.13-14.text: Israelites celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles with joy

DEU.16.15-15.text: Israelites feast for seven days with complete joy

DEU.16.16-17.text: All men must appear before the LORD three times a year

DEU.17.2-4.text: Israelites must check reports of worship of other gods

DEU.17.5-7.text: Two or three witnesses are needed to put a person to death

DEU.17.8-9.text: Israelites take hard cases to the priests and the judge

DEU.17.10-11.text: Israelites must obey the verdict of the priests and judge

DEU.17.12-13.text: A man who refuses to obey the priest or judge must die

DEU.17.14-15.text: Israel may appoint a king chosen by God from Israelites

DEU.17.16-17.text: The king must not collect too many horses, wives or gold

DEU.17.18-19.text: The king must write and read God’s law all his life

DEU.17.20-20.text: Reading the law keeps the king humble and obedient

DEU.18.1-2.text: The Levites have no land and eat the offerings to the LORD

DEU.18.3-5.text: Israelites must give the priests a share and firstfruits

DEU.18.6-8.text: A Levite from any town may serve at the chosen place

DEU.18.9-11.text: Israelites must not practice sorcery like the nations

DEU.18.12-14.text: God drives out the nations; Israel must be blameless

DEU.18.15-16.text: God will raise up a prophet like Moses for Israel

DEU.18.17-19.text: God will give his words to the prophet; Israel must listen

DEU.18.20-21.text: A prophet who speaks what God did not command must die

DEU.18.22-22.text: A message that does not come true is not from God

DEU.19.1-3.text: Israel must set apart three cities and build roads

DEU.19.4-5.text: A man who kills by accident may flee to a city

DEU.19.6-7.text: Cities protect a man who killed by accident from revenge

DEU.19.8-10.text: Israel must add three more cities if God enlarges the land

DEU.19.11-13.text: Elders must hand a murderer over to the avenger of blood

DEU.19.14-14.text: Israelites must not move a neighbor’s boundary marker

DEU.19.15-16.text: A charge needs two or three witnesses

DEU.19.17-19.text: Judges must punish a false witness as he planned

DEU.19.20-21.text: Israel must show no pity to a false witness

DEU.20.1-1.text: Israel must not fear a larger army; God is with Israel

DEU.20.2-4.text: The priest tells the army that God will fight for Israel

DEU.20.5-5.text: Officers send home a man with a new house

DEU.20.6-7.text: Officers send home men with a new vineyard or a bride

DEU.20.8-9.text: Officers send home fearful men and appoint commanders

DEU.20.10-11.text: Israel must offer peace to a city before attacking

DEU.20.12-13.text: Israel must besiege a city that refuses peace

DEU.20.14-15.text: Israel may take the women, children and goods of far cities

DEU.20.16-18.text: Israel must completely destroy the nations in the land

DEU.20.19-20.text: Israel must not cut down fruit trees during a siege

DEU.21.1-2.text: Elders measure from a slain man to the nearby cities

DEU.21.3-4.text: The nearest city’s elders break a heifer’s neck in a valley

DEU.21.5-5.text: The priests come forward to settle disputes

DEU.21.6-7.text: The elders wash hands and say the city is innocent

DEU.21.8-9.text: The elders ask God to accept atonement for Israel

DEU.21.10-12.text: A man may marry a beautiful captive woman

DEU.21.13-14.text: A captive wife mourns a month and must not be sold

DEU.21.18-19.text: Parents bring a rebellious son to the city elders

DEU.21.20-21.text: Parents accuse a rebellious son and the city stones him

DEU.21.22-23.text: Cursed Is Anyone Hung on a Tree

DEU.22.1-2.text: Israelites must return a brother’s lost animal

DEU.22.3-4.text: Israelites must return lost things and lift fallen animals

DEU.22.5-5.text: Men and women must not wear each other’s clothing

DEU.22.6-7.text: Israelites must let a mother bird go when taking her young

DEU.22.8-8.text: Israelites must build a railing around a new roof

DEU.22.9-11.text: Israelites must not mix different seeds, animals or cloth

DEU.22.12-12.text: Israelites must put tassels on the corners of a cloak

DEU.22.13-14.text: A husband accuses his new wife of shameful conduct

DEU.22.15-15.text: Parents bring proof of a daughter’s virginity to elders

DEU.22.16-17.text: Parents defend a daughter before the city elders

DEU.22.18-19.text: The elders punish and fine the man who accused his wife

DEU.22.20-21.text: If the accusation is true, the bride is stoned

DEU.22.22-22.text: A man and another man’s wife who lie together must die

DEU.22.23-24.text: Both die when a man sleeps with an engaged woman in a city

DEU.22.25-27.text: Only the man dies for attacking an engaged woman in a field

DEU.22.28-29.text: A man who seizes a virgin must pay her father and marry her

DEU.22.30-30.text: A man must not marry his father’s wife

DEU.23.1-2.text: Some people may not enter the LORD’s assembly

DEU.23.3-4.text: Ammonites and Moabites may not enter the LORD’s assembly

DEU.23.5-6.text: God turned Balaam’s curse into a blessing for Israel

DEU.23.7-8.text: Israelites must not despise Edomites or Egyptians

DEU.23.9-11.text: An unclean man must stay outside the camp until evening

DEU.23.12-14.text: Israelites must keep the camp clean because God is there

DEU.23.15-16.text: Israelites must not return an escaped slave to his master

DEU.23.17-18.text: God rejects shrine prostitutes and prostitutes’ wages

DEU.23.19-20.text: Israelites must not charge interest to a brother

DEU.23.21-23.text: Israelites must keep vows made to God without delay

DEU.23.24-25.text: Israelites may eat grapes and grain in a neighbor’s field

DEU.24.1-2.text: A man may divorce his wife with a written certificate

DEU.24.3-4.text: A man may not remarry a wife who married another

DEU.24.5-5.text: A newly married man need not go to war for a year

DEU.24.6-6.text: Israelites must not take millstones as security for a debt

DEU.24.7-7.text: A kidnapper of a fellow Israelite must die

DEU.24.8-9.text: Israel must follow the priests’ teaching on skin diseases

DEU.24.10-11.text: Lenders must wait outside for the security

DEU.24.12-13.text: Lenders must return a poor man’s cloak by sunset

DEU.24.14-15.text: Employers must pay poor workers each day before sunset

DEU.24.16-16.text: Each person dies only for his own sin

DEU.24.17-18.text: Israel must treat foreigners, orphans and widows fairly

DEU.24.19-20.text: Israelites must leave grain and olives for the needy

DEU.24.21-22.text: Israelites must leave some grapes for the needy

DEU.25.1-2.text: Judges must decide disputes and punish the guilty

DEU.25.3-3.text: A guilty man may receive no more than forty lashes

DEU.25.4-4.text: Israelites must not muzzle an ox that treads grain

DEU.25.5-6.text: A brother must marry his dead brother’s childless widow

DEU.25.7-8.text: A widow may go to the elders if her brother-in-law refuses

DEU.25.9-10.text: The widow shames a brother-in-law who refuses to marry

DEU.25.11-12.text: The punishment for a wife who grabs a man in a fight

DEU.25.13-14.text: Israelites must not use two different weights or measures

DEU.25.15-16.text: Israelites must use honest weights and measures

DEU.26.1-2.text: Israelites must bring firstfruits to God’s chosen place

DEU.26.3-4.text: An Israelite tells the priest he has entered the land

DEU.26.5-5.text: The Israelite recalls Israel’s ancestor in Egypt

DEU.26.6-7.text: The Israelite says God heard Israel’s cry in Egypt

DEU.26.8-9.text: The Israelite says God brought Israel out to this land

DEU.26.10-11.text: The Israelite presents the firstfruits and rejoices

DEU.26.12-13.text: In the third year Israelites give the tithe to the needy

DEU.26.14-15.text: The Israelite says he obeyed and asks God’s blessing

DEU.26.16-17.text: Israel promises to walk in God’s ways and obey him

DEU.26.18-19.text: God declares that Israel is his treasured people

DEU.27.1-3.text: Israel must write the law on plastered stones

DEU.27.4-5.text: Israel must build a stone altar on Mount Ebal

DEU.27.6-8.text: Israel must offer sacrifices and rejoice at the altar

DEU.27.9-10.text: Moses and the priests tell Israel to obey God

DEU.27.11-12.text: Six tribes stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people

DEU.27.13-14.text: Six tribes stand on Mount Ebal to speak the curse

DEU.27.15-15.text: The Levites curse anyone who secretly makes an idol

DEU.27.16-17.text: Curses on dishonoring parents and moving boundary stones

DEU.27.18-19.text: Curses for misleading a blind man and denying justice

DEU.27.20-21.text: Curses on sex with a father’s wife or with an animal

DEU.27.22-23.text: Curses on sex with a sister or a mother-in-law

DEU.27.24-25.text: Curses on killing a neighbor in secret or for a bribe

DEU.27.26-26.text: Curse on anyone who does not obey the words of this law

DEU.28.1-2.text: God will bless Israel above all nations if the people obey

DEU.28.3-4.text: Blessings on the people, the fields and the animals

DEU.28.5-6.text: Blessings on the people’s food and on coming and going

DEU.28.7-8.text: God will defeat Israel’s enemies and bless the land

DEU.28.9-10.text: God will make obedient Israel his holy people

DEU.28.11-12.text: God will make Israel prosper and send rain

DEU.28.13-14.text: Israel will lead, not follow, if the people obey God

DEU.28.15-15.text: Curses will come if Israel does not obey God

DEU.28.16-17.text: Curses on the city, the country and the food supply

DEU.28.18-19.text: Curses on the people’s children, crops and animals

DEU.28.20-21.text: God will send confusion and plague because Israel left him

DEU.28.22-22.text: God will strike Israel with disease, drought and blight

DEU.28.23-24.text: Drought will make the sky bronze and the earth iron

DEU.28.25-26.text: Israel will be defeated and become a horror to nations

DEU.28.27-29.text: God will send boils, madness and blindness on Israel

DEU.28.30-31.text: Enemies will take the people’s homes, fields and animals

DEU.28.32-32.text: Israel’s children will be given to another nation

DEU.28.33-35.text: A foreign people will eat the crops and oppress Israel

DEU.28.36-37.text: Israel and its king will be driven to a foreign land

DEU.28.38-39.text: Locusts and worms will destroy the crops and vineyards

DEU.28.40-41.text: Olives will fall and children will go into captivity

DEU.28.42-44.text: Foreigners will rise above Israel and become the head

DEU.28.45-46.text: The curses will last as a sign for Israel forever

DEU.28.47-48.text: Israel will serve enemies for not serving God with joy

DEU.28.49-51.text: A fierce nation from far away will destroy Israel

DEU.28.52-53.text: Siege will drive parents to eat children

DEU.28.54-55.text: A gentle man will refuse to share his children’s flesh

DEU.28.56-57.text: A gentle woman will secretly eat her children in the siege

DEU.28.58-59.text: God will send terrible diseases if Israel disobeys

DEU.28.60-62.text: God will bring Egypt’s diseases on disobedient Israel

DEU.28.63-64.text: God will scatter Israel from the land among the nations

DEU.28.65-66.text: Scattered Israel will have no rest and always be afraid

DEU.28.67-68.text: Israel will dread each day and return to Egypt as slaves

DEU.29.1-1.text: God makes another covenant with Israel in Moab

DEU.29.2-4.text: Moses reminds Israel of what God did in Egypt

DEU.29.5-6.text: Israel’s clothes did not wear out in the wilderness

DEU.29.7-9.text: Israel defeated Sihon and Og; Moses urges obedience

DEU.29.10-11.text: All Israel stands before God, including foreigners

DEU.29.12-13.text: God makes Israel his people by the covenant and oath

DEU.29.14-16.text: The covenant is for Israel and for later generations

DEU.29.17-19.text: Moses warns Israel against turning to idols

DEU.29.20-21.text: God will punish anyone who turns to other gods

DEU.29.22-24.text: Nations will see Israel’s land ruined like Sodom

DEU.29.25-26.text: People will say Israel left God for other gods

DEU.29.27-28.text: God uproots Israel from the land in great anger

DEU.29.29-29.text: God keeps secrets; Israel must follow what is revealed

DEU.30.1-3.text: God will bring Israel back if the people return to him

DEU.30.4-5.text: God will gather Israel from far places to the land

DEU.30.6-8.text: God will change Israel’s hearts to love him

DEU.30.9-10.text: God will bless Israel again if the people obey him

DEU.30.11-12.text: God’s commandment is not too hard or far away

DEU.30.13-14.text: God’s word is near Israel, in mouth and heart

DEU.30.15-16.text: Moses offers Israel life or death: love God and live

DEU.30.17-18.text: Israel will perish if the people worship other gods

DEU.30.19-20.text: Moses calls Israel to choose life and love God

DEU.31.1-3.text: Moses, age 120, says God will lead Israel across

DEU.31.4-6.text: Moses urges Israel to be strong; God will not leave

DEU.31.7-8.text: Moses tells Joshua to be strong and not afraid

DEU.31.9-11.text: Moses orders the law read to Israel every seven years

DEU.31.12-13.text: All the people must hear the law and learn to fear God

DEU.31.14-15.text: God tells Moses to bring Joshua to the Tent of Meeting

DEU.31.16-16.text: God tells Moses the Israelites will worship other gods

DEU.31.17-18.text: God says he will abandon Israel because of idols

DEU.31.19-20.text: God tells Moses to teach Israel a song as a witness

DEU.31.21-21.text: The song will speak against Israel when troubles come

DEU.31.22-23.text: Moses writes the song, and God commissions Joshua

DEU.31.24-26.text: Moses tells the Levites to put the law beside the ark

DEU.31.27-29.text: Moses says Israel will rebel after his death

DEU.32.1-2.text: Moses calls heaven and earth to hear his song

DEU.32.3-4.text: Moses praises God as the faithful and just Rock

DEU.32.5-6.text: Moses says Israel has been unfaithful to God its Father

DEU.32.7-8.text: Moses reminds Israel that God set the nations’ borders

DEU.32.9-10.text: God chose Israel and cared for Israel in the desert

DEU.32.11-12.text: God carried Israel like an eagle carries its young

DEU.32.13-13.text: God gave Israel good food from the land

DEU.32.14-14.text: God gave Israel rich food and fine wine

DEU.32.15-16.text: Israel became fat, left God and served foreign gods

DEU.32.17-18.text: Israel offered sacrifices to demons and forgot God

DEU.32.19-20.text: God rejects his sons and daughters for unfaithfulness

DEU.32.21-21.text: God will make Israel jealous through another nation

DEU.32.22-22.text: God’s anger burns like a fire over the earth

DEU.32.23-24.text: God will send hunger, plague and wild animals on Israel

DEU.32.25-26.text: War and fear will strike young and old in Israel

DEU.32.27-27.text: God spares Israel so enemies will not boast

DEU.32.28-29.text: Moses says Israel has no wisdom or understanding

DEU.32.30-31.text: Israel’s defeat came because God gave Israel up

DEU.32.32-32.text: Moses says the enemy’s vine is poisonous and bitter

DEU.32.33-34.text: The enemy’s wine is like deadly snake poison

DEU.32.35-35.text: God says he will repay, and disaster is near

DEU.32.36-36.text: God will have mercy on his people when strength is gone

DEU.32.37-38.text: God asks where the false gods are to help Israel

DEU.32.39-40.text: God says he alone is God and controls life and death

DEU.32.41-41.text: God will punish his enemies with his sword

DEU.32.42-42.text: God’s sword will destroy his enemies

DEU.32.43-43.text: The nations should rejoice because God will avenge his people

DEU.32.44-45.text: Moses and Joshua recite the song to the people

DEU.32.46-47.text: Moses tells Israel to teach the law to their children

DEU.32.48-49.text: God tells Moses to go up Mount Nebo and see Canaan

DEU.32.50-52.text: God says Moses will die and not enter the land

DEU.33.1-2.text: Moses begins to bless Israel and speaks of the LORD’s coming

DEU.33.3-4.text: Moses says the LORD loves his people and gave them the law

DEU.33.5-6.text: The LORD is King; Moses blesses Reuben

DEU.33.7-7.text: Moses asks the LORD to help the tribe of Judah

DEU.33.8-8.text: Moses blesses Levi, who was tested at Massah

DEU.33.9-9.text: Levi was faithful to the LORD’s word above his family

DEU.33.10-10.text: Levi will teach God’s law and offer sacrifices

DEU.33.11-11.text: Moses asks the LORD to bless Levi and defeat his enemies

DEU.33.12-12.text: Moses blesses Benjamin, who rests safe in God

DEU.33.13-13.text: Moses asks the LORD to bless Joseph’s land

DEU.33.14-15.text: Moses asks for good harvests and rich hills for Joseph

DEU.33.16-16.text: Moses asks God’s favor to rest on Joseph

DEU.33.17-17.text: Moses says Ephraim and Manasseh will be strong like a bull

DEU.33.20-20.text: Moses blesses Gad, who is strong like a lion

DEU.33.21-21.text: Gad chose the best land and did the LORD’s justice

DEU.33.22-22.text: Moses says the tribe of Dan is like a lion’s cub

DEU.33.23-23.text: Moses blesses Naphtali with the LORD’s favor and land

DEU.33.24-25.text: Moses blesses Asher with favor, safety and strength

DEU.33.26-26.text: Moses says no god is like the God of Israel

DEU.33.27-27.text: God is Israel’s safe home and drives out the enemy

DEU.33.28-28.text: Israel lives safely in a land of grain and wine

DEU.33.29-29.text: Moses says Israel is blessed because the LORD saves it

DEU.34.1-3.text: The LORD shows Moses the whole land from Mount Nebo

DEU.34.4-6.text: Moses dies in Moab and the LORD buries him

DEU.34.7-8.text: Moses dies at 120 and Israel mourns thirty days

DEU.34.9-9.text: Joshua is full of wisdom and Israel obeys him

DEU.34.10-12.text: No prophet in Israel was ever like Moses
